children: Meta Platforms' capital-expenditure plans failed to soothe investors concerned the AI boom is slowing, Quilter Cheviot's Ben Barringer writes. The social-media company left the high end of its capital-expenditure guide for the year unchanged at $140 billion, while raising the low end by $5 billion to $135 billion. The company didn't provide detail on its 2027 spending plans but said it will continue "investing aggressively." The lack of a significant raise means "there's not much there for the AI CapEx trade," Barringer says, adding that some investors might have thought there would be a another big increase. Meta shares fall 1.75% amid a broader AI selloff, as Nasdaq futures drop 1.8%. (josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)
